transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I get stuck in front of the mirror or looking at photos of myself, trying to fix how I look, and it’s starting to mess with my work and my runs. It's gotten to the point where I just can't seem to shake it on my own anymore.
When you look in the mirror, are you primarily concerned about your body weight and shape, or is your focus on a specific feature like your face, skin, or hair?

No, it’s not about my weight or shape at all; it’s really about my face. I look at myself and just see how battered and crooked it is, like my nose is bent and my jaw is completely off. Plus, my skin just looks like old, worn-out leather, and I can't stop focusing on it.

Aside from focusing on your appearance, do you experience other unwanted, repetitive thoughts or feel driven to perform rituals, such as constant handwashing, checking locks, or needing things arranged in a specific order?
No, I don't have any of those other habits like handwashing or checking locks. Everything I'm struggling with is strictly focused on my appearance and trying to fix how my face looks.
How long have you been experiencing these intense worries about your face and skin? Has this been going on for at least six months?

Yes, it's been going on for much longer than six months, probably about two years now. It started gradually when my company shifted to more public-facing projects and people started posting photos of us on social media, and it has been a constant struggle ever since.
When you look at these flaws on your face, do you believe with absolute certainty that they are as severe as you see them, or do you think it's possible your mind might be exaggerating these issues?
I'm not really sure. To me, it feels completely real and obvious when I look in the mirror, but I haven't really thought about whether my mind is playing tricks on me or exaggerating it.
When family or friends tell you that they don't see these flaws on your face, do you believe them, or do you feel they are lying to you or hiding the truth?

I'm not really sure, it's just hard to believe them when I see it so clearly myself. I don't think they're lying, but I just can't shake the feeling that they're just trying to be nice and spare my feelings.
When you are out in public, do you feel certain that strangers are staring at you, whispering, or making fun of your face?
I don't really think strangers are staring or whispering about me specifically. But I still worry constantly about how they might judge my appearance if they happen to look at me closely.
Have you ever consulted a dermatologist or plastic surgeon about these concerns, and if so, how did you react to their medical opinion?
No, I've never gone to see a dermatologist or a plastic surgeon for any of this. I've just been trying to deal with it on my own, mostly by trying to fix things in the mirror.

Apart from your concerns about your appearance, do you have any other strong beliefs that others find hard to accept, such as feeling that you are being watched, plotted against, or that something unusual is happening to your body internally?

No, I don't have any feelings like that at all. I don't feel like anyone is plotting against me, and there's nothing wrong with my body internally. My distress is strictly about how my face and skin look on the outside in photos and the mirror.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in their physical appearance (specifically their face, nose, jaw, and skin) that are not noticeable or appear slight to others. This preoccupation has lasted for approximately two years, causing significant distress and impairment in social and occupational functioning (messing with work and runs). The patient engages in repetitive behaviors (checking and trying to fix their appearance in the mirror and photos). These symptoms align with Body Dysmorphic Disorder, which is classified under F45.2 (Hypochondriacal disorder) in ICD-10.
